audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradict their own whys[]. Level 1 is marked Skill while its why says he chips you for free with no combo to answer; Levels 2 and 3 are given to Rumble while their whys call them 'your one clean punish window' and 'You still out-trade him here'; Levels 4-5 and 6 are marked Skill while their whys say his overheat out-DPSes your healing and that The Equalizer zones you off the wave entirely.
audit.why: Rumble's power curve is heat, not levels: with one Flamespitter point he cannot reach Danger Zone reliably, which is exactly the Level 2-3 window Maokai owns. From a second point onward the burn beats Sap Magic, and at 6 a flame wall across the wave denies both his CS and his sustain. The 44.26% win rate matches a lane that is his everywhere except that short window.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3 and 4 set to Rumble (3/10); rows 1 and 2 set to Maokai (6/10), in both layers. That is the packet chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says The Equalizer 'lands two AOE lines across the wave'. It is one wall of flame, not two lines. The same entry and wants.foe[2] also write the ability as 'His Equalizer' / 'Equalizer' rather than its actual name, The Equalizer.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Rumble fires off a group of rockets, creating a wall of flames that damages and slows enemies.' A player told to expect two separate lines will misjudge where the safe ground is — there is one wall, and the dodge is to leave it, not to thread between lines.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now says 'lays a wall of flame' and uses The Equalizer; wants.foe[2] uses The Equalizer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon's magic resist shred is never mentioned anywhere, while the file's headline advice in tldr, winCon and dosFull[1] is 'Build MR'. dontsFull[0] and dontsFull[1] both carry filler descriptions unrelated to their titles.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist on hit and he carries two charges with only 0.5s between them, so he can strip a chunk of the exact stat the page tells you to stack before the burn even starts. That does not make MR wrong — it makes flat MR alone insufficient, and it is why the sustain-and-MR item is the right shape rather than raw resistances. Flamespitter also burns for 3 seconds in a cone, which is what makes standing in it so costly.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d states Flamespitter's 3-second cone; dontsFull[1].d states the Electro Harpoon MR shred.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page tracks Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining cooldown. Scrap Shield is a flat 6 seconds.
audit.why: A 6-second shield cannot be the cooldown a lane is played around — it is back before Maokai's W (14s at rank 1) is. The cooldowns that actually gate this matchup are Flamespitter at 10/9/8/7/6s and, more than any of them, his heat bar. I have written the 6s figure in so the reader can see for themselves that baiting it is not a plan, but the focus.text change itself is a page-level call I did not make unilaterally.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now states the 6s. See questionsForUser — focus.text may want to move to Flamespitter.

audit.why: Two derived-flag misfires in rumble.json, both contradicted by Riot's own descriptions and therefore not used anywhere: Scrap Shield is flagged 'knockup' and 'terrain' when the text describes only a shield plus a speed burst, and The Equalizer is flagged 'projectile' when it creates a wall of flame. The mirror audit on rumble reached the same conclusion independently.
audit.corrected: No edit — recorded so a later pass does not add a Scrap Shield knockup that does not exist.

notes: Two real errors beyond the chart: The Equalizer was described as 'two AOE lines' when it is a single wall of flame, and the page's headline 'Build MR' advice never mentioned that Electro Harpoon shreds magic resist on hit with two charges. Also confirmed the mirror's finding that rumble.json's Scrap Shield knockup/terrain flags and Equalizer projectile flag are tooltip-parsing misfires contradicted by Riot's text — nothing here relies on them.
